messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In lions, one of the most striking examples of a dominant genetic trait is the development of the mane in adult male lions. The presence and size of the mane are largely governed by genes that respond to testosterone levels; the alleles that promote mane growth are dominant over those that do not. This means that if a male lion inherits at least one copy of the mane-promoting allele from either parent, it will develop a mane (though its size and darkness can still vary depending on other modifiers).
